problem: The new owner wanted to cut costs and move faster, and advertisers were already pulling back.
title: Twitter lays off about half its staff after the Musk acquisition
context: Elon Musk completed his $44 billion acquisition of Twitter in late October 2022.
decision_made: Lay off roughly half of about 7,500 employees within about a week of the takeover.
action_taken: Cuts were made company-wide; within days the company reached out to dozens of laid-off employees asking them to return.
observed_outcome: Reports said some employees were laid off by mistake and were asked back; several major advertisers suspended spending. Longer-term results were not found in the sources used.
lessons: Fast, broad cuts can remove people the company still needs and may have to be partly reversed.
limitations: Only the immediate aftermath was covered. Staff counts differ by source and the longer-term advertiser and business effects were not checked.

claims.claim_text: Twitter laid off about half of its staff within a week of Musk's takeover.
Twitter asked dozens of laid-off employees to return, some reportedly laid off by mistake.
